extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal foundation models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It comprises 11.5K multimodal questions collected from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, Tech & Engineering), 30 subjects, 183 subfields, and 30 heterogeneous image types.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collection occurred in three stages: first, university majors/subjects were selected based on whether visual inputs are commonly adopted to provide valuable information. Second, over 50 university students (including coauthors) specializing in these majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks, quizzes, online resources, and lecture materials, or create new questions based on expertise. Data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution were avoided, and questions without immediately available answers were prioritized. This initially yielded 13K questions. Quality control steps included duplicate detection via lexical overlap and URL similarity, format/typo checking, and filtering out ~10% of questions deemed 'very easy', resulting in 11.5K questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, major textbooks, lecture materials, and free online resources across 30 subjects and 6 disciplines.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two steps of data cleaning and filtering were conducted: 1) Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to flag and eliminate duplicates. 2) Formatting and typos were checked and standardized. 3) Problems were categorized into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), and approximately 10% of questions categorized as 'very easy' were excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators identified or created multimodal questions across 30 subjects ensuring all questions contained images, met college-level difficulty, were in English, and were unambiguous. Annotators recorded question text, question type (multiple-choice or open-ended), answer options, correct answer, image types, difficulty level, and explanation (if available). A secondary review team vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence, and ambiguous cases were discussed and resolved collaboratively in team meetings.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface developed for data annotation and verification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Ambiguities or unclear data instances were flagged for a detailed review process and collaboratively examined in team meetings to establish a standardized approach. Suspected duplicates and format deviations were verified and corrected across multiple co-authors.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: A team of over 50 college students (including coauthors) specializing in the 30 targeted university subjects/majors from various disciplines.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark includes a live-updating leaderboard at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard, with version tracking documented in a version change log.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information to ensure compliance with privacy laws and ethical standards.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Evaluates progress toward 'Expert AGI' (reaching at least the 90th percentile of skilled adults in diverse tasks), which could mark the substitution threshold of machine intelligence for human labor and result in potential risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors state that the manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI because there is no direct mapping between benchmark performance and the 90th percentile of skilled adults, and college exams are not the only tasks an AGI must tackle. Additionally, the manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Zero-shot and few-shot evaluation and benchmarking of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) on college-level multimodal understanding and reasoning across diverse disciplines.
